title: Learning ninth, minor and diminished chords with a white friend, George Bourne
summary: Vincent and a white boy studied orchestration parts to work out nine, diminished and minor chords; he describes his friend George Bourne, who fixed electronics and stayed home.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: You're going to tell us about those six cars.

I didn't tell you about it, huh? And I thought, you see, me and a white boy, we'd come up together, and we could play a little bit, but the next I learned him how to play. And we used to sit down together and study and go with them cars. Some of them nine cars, they go for minor, you see. They go for diminished cars. Sixty the same way, you see. Let me see, B flat, diminished, six. B flat nine. We make that B flat and come find it's a minor cars, you know? It's a way to get it, two bandages, sometimes two guitars. It ain't all that in the book, but since we moved here, it got lost, you know? We must have thrown it away, you know?
What was the name of the book?

Oh, we take it from the parts of the orchestration music. You know, we'd catch it like that. We'd make them cars to find out what they is, you see. If it's a nine car, we'd make a nine car to find out what it is. Sometimes it'd be a diminished car, it'd be a seven car, it'd be a minor car. That's the way some of them call for it, you see.

And the fifth car, I forget, they called it B flat seven. The white boy? Fifth. He said, what was that boy name which used to wake with you, the white boy? He named George Bourne. He don't play no more. He got a good head on it. The boy taking a single house, him and his sister. He made five depositments out of single house. He pitched a radio, television, and everything. And he didn't want to work at nothing no more. He said, he's tired, he wanted to rest, you know? He had a smart head. I didn't get that television. Then he turned fish when he got out, you know? He wouldn't try my knicker. He picked all my cars. I learned to him how to make all them cars. He went with a band once. I put him with a band, but he couldn't get along with musicians, you know? He don't like to go nowhere. He was going to chase nines and the other way, you know, going nowhere but just sit around his house and work, you know? Then he'd give up pictures, television, and radio and things like that. He'd fix electricity. Fix anything. Fix all the mobiles, anything. Mind energy for his friends, you know? And he don't bother with it. Don't put down the gas, neither. No, he said, if he's been mad, he's been built too long ago to talk about it.
He said, what? He said, see, I got mad, he's been built too long ago to talk about it. He never had no money in her.
